scope: String/argv semantic boundary; research reference experiment only, not product runtime PASS
observed_anchors: Current canonical source-to-single-VM gate admits String literal/return but explicitly rejects String parameters.
Current merged CM-TERM bridge has an explicit typed hostcall signature but direct Clay String argv remains open.
POSIX/Linux exec argv elements are null-terminated character strings; embedded NUL therefore cannot be represented as one host argv element.
generated_reality: Clay String should remain an internal length-delimited semantic value; the Linux process boundary should encode String->argv explicitly and reject embedded NUL before any host process effect.
counter_reality: If Clay String is implicitly modeled as a host C-string everywhere, internal values can silently truncate or backend-local argv restrictions can leak backward into language semantics.

unusual_experiment.name: embedded_nul_string_to_linux_argv_boundary
unusual_experiment.baseline: Length-delimited internal bytes for ENTITYOS_STRING round-trip and execute as a normal /usr/bin/printf argv element.
unusual_experiment.intervention: Insert one embedded NUL byte into the internal UTF-8 byte sequence before Linux argv encoding.

falsifier: A future canonical Clay String/argv implementation fails this constraint if internal String silently truncates at NUL, or if the Linux argv adapter accepts an embedded-NUL String without a deterministic pre-effect rejection.
test_obligation: When direct Clay String argv is admitted, add one canonical source->TypedIR->single-VM->Linux-boundary gate that preserves ordinary String values and rejects embedded NUL before hostcall execution/receipt creation; do not treat this reference-model result as product evidence.
